domain_test: The decisive step is how an index fund's 13F holdings behave: an index or ETF sponsor holds the index weight, so in shares it holds a fixed slice of each constituent's float, scaled by its own creations, and its share count in a name moves when that company issues, buys back or tenders while an active manager's does not; completing a quarter still inside its 45-day window has to move each sponsor still due with each name's own count; with another field's nouns there is no float to track, no creation mechanism and no filing window.

driver: One class of holder keeps a fixed fraction of each unit rather than a fixed amount, so when a unit's size changes that class's amount in it moves with it, and the class's common change is a change in the fraction, the same in every unit; completing the holders not yet reported in a still-open period with one amount change per class pooled across units misstates the units whose size moved, carrying every class as a fraction misstates the units whose missing holders keep amounts, and the basis a filed back-test criterion selects moves each missing holder of that class with its own unit's size and the class's change in fraction while every other class keeps its amount.
driver_concrete: At the 3 February 2023 extract the December 13F window (deadline 14 February) is open and OM-4 s.2 files the estimand (every manager that reports holdings for the quarter, the 129 still due included, their holdings estimated) and the criterion that selects the basis (closest on the September window at the same day, by the largest miss across the twelve names); an index or ETF sponsor holds a fixed slice of each company's float, so its shares in a name move with that name's count (OTF's October follow-on +4.6 per cent, FENN's shares issued for an acquisition +4.8, ABBB's tender -5.4, the buybacks at WHII, JEMS, AMRB and NOPR, GLI's July follow-on +5.0, SAF's July tender -4.0) on top of its creations (its stake in every name +5.5 per cent a quarter), while every other register type is flat in aggregate in shares; the selected basis grows each sponsor still due by the change its filed peers show in that name (equivalently its September stake grown by the sponsors' stake growth), which puts OTF, a quarter of it held by sponsors still due, at 80.4, while the sponsors' change pooled across the names in shares (about 4.5 per cent) leaves OTF at about 79.2, and carrying every manager's stake or one rate for everyone flags FENN, whose managers still due are multi-strategy funds.
stump: A competent solver executes OM-4 literally, sees that the index and ETF sponsors that have filed grew their share holdings while every other register type held flat, grows each of the 129 managers still due by its own type's change pooled across the twelve names, sees that basis beat every other it builds in the September back-test (largest miss about 0.66 points against 1.0 for the all-filer change, 1.4 for flat carry and 2.6 per name), and flags WHII, GLI, JEMS and SAF with OTF at about 79.2; the step that lands it there is treating the sponsors' change as one factor for every name, when an index sponsor holds a fixed slice of each company, so in shares it moves with that name's share count as well as with its creations: OTF issued about 4.6 per cent more shares in October and its sponsors still due, 23 per cent of OTF, took their slice, which the two filed sponsors' OTF holdings show (up about 10.4 per cent against 4.5 pooled), so the basis the filed criterion selects grows each sponsor still due by the change its filed peers show in that name (largest miss about 0.04), which puts OTF at 80.4 and keeps FENN, whose managers still due are multi-strategy funds, at 79.6.

differentiation.task445: Loop 1 (lineage) moved each missing reporter by its class's common drift pooled across the units, which round 3 landed; loop 2's decisive move is that the drifting class holds fractions of each unit, so a class change pooled across units in amounts is wrong unit by unit wherever a unit's size moved, and the selected basis applies the class's change in fraction with each unit's own size change; the loop 1 basis is loop 2's stump rung.
differentiation.task181: task181 nowcasts how much of a fortnight is still in transit, by each reporting route's own arrival delay (how much is missing); task445 knows exactly which holders are missing and turns on what they now hold: the missing index sponsors hold a fixed slice of each company, so they are moved with each name's share count and the sponsors' stake growth, not with their own history and not with a factor pooled across names, a basis a filed back-test criterion selects.
differentiation.task107: task107 v4 carries each unit forward past a dated step (a pay rise at a service anniversary) that earlier entrants show in the history, so its decisive step is when the step takes effect against the forward window; task445 has no dated event: one reporter class's holdings drift at a common rate every quarter (creations), measured on that class's filed peers in the same open period, and the decisive step is completing each missing reporter by its own class's drift, which a filed back-test criterion selects over flat carry and over any pooled rate.
differentiation.task446: task446 backs a forward count out of a screen's flagged share through error rates that hold across years while its yield moves with the base rate; task445 completes an open filing window holder by holder, and its decisive step is the quantity the missing index sponsors conserve (a slice of each company, moving with each name's share count), not a screen's yield against a base rate.

lineage.fate: in-house round 2 missed at flat carry; in-house round 3 (2026-10-11) landed the call on the register-type change pooled across the names (0.042 points in OM-4 s.2's back-test against 0.60 for the all-filer change); hardened in loop 2 by making the index sponsors' holdings follow each name's share count, so that basis is the stump rung
lineage.driver: A period still open at the extract is completed for the reporters not yet in by carrying each from its last report, but that report is stale for the class of reporter whose holdings drift every period at a common rate, so each missing reporter is moved by the drift its own class already shows among those that have reported, the basis a filed back-test criterion selects; flat carry misplaces the unit whose missing reporters are of the drifting class, and any single rate for every missing reporter misplaces the unit whose missing reporters are not.

lineage.fate: portal round 1 (2026-10-11): rubric average 52, determinism QC failed (answer_contradicts_files, golden_wrong): OM-4 s.2 named the filers for the period and filed no completion, so the literal reading counted only the reports on file; the driver also collided with task181 (task446 pre-flight); hardened in loop 1 by filing the estimand and a basis-selection criterion and moving the decisive step to the basis
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is the part of a period's total still held by reporters whose reports have not arrived at the extract; because slow reporters concentrate in some units and not others, it has to be completed reporter by reporter from each one's last report, and reading the arrived reports as the total, or scaling every unit by one aggregate completion share, misstates exactly the units whose holders report late and changes which units cross the threshold.
